description: Render the WORKFLOW.md prompt template against the normalized issue and attempt. Templates use Liquid-compatible syntax (Section 5.4); the variable set (issue, attempt) and the strict-failure semantics are the normative contract, and an engine that is not Liquid-compatible maps these to its equivalent. Strict mode: an unknown variable and an unknown filter MUST fail rendering, and Section 5.5 makes the error class a REQUIRED spelling, so the class asserted below is the one a conforming implementation reports. A class names the condition, not the stage that detected it (Section 5.5): an engine that resolves filter names while parsing still reports an unknown filter as template_render_error, and template_parse_error is reported only for a body that is not well-formed template syntax. Templates are single-line and use delimiters rather than inter-token whitespace so the expected output does not depend on an engine's whitespace-control behavior.
given: { template: string, issue: object, attempt: integer | null }
expect: { rendered: string } on success, or { error: string } naming the error class on failure

vectors.description: A known issue field renders as its value.
Several known fields render in place.

vectors.description: The attempt variable renders when present as an integer (retry/continuation run).
Strict mode: a reference to a variable that is neither issue nor attempt MUST fail rendering (Section 5.4).

Strict mode: an unknown filter MUST fail rendering (Section 5.4). The class is template_render_error even where the engine resolves filter names while parsing, because a class names the condition rather than the stage that detected it (Section 5.5).

A body that is not well-formed template syntax is template_parse_error (Section 5.5). This is the iterate-labels template with its closing tag removed, so the only difference from the passing vector is the malformation.
